course_name_original: ΕΜΥ - 344 Transport Phenomena in Materials Science

learning_outcomes.text: Have familiarity with Fourier's, Newton's and Fick's Laws for heat, momentum and mass transfer.
Be able to establish conservation equations and necessary initial and boundary conditions, and decide on sufficient assumptions.
Solve in detail some simplified cases.
Recognize qualitative solutions of complex cases and understand temperature, velocity and concentration distributions.
Apply the above to basic problems of heat, momentum and mass transfer in materials e.g. insulation, Newtonian fluid flow, evaporation.

Analysis and synthesis of data and information using the necessary (theoretical, and basic computational and experimental) technologies. Develop critical thinking to select appropriate assumptions for problem solving.
Work in an interdisciplinary environment. Transport phenomena concern various properties of materials, materials of various phases and are applied in a wide range of cases.

Development of synthetical thinking. Transport phenomena are presented in Nature as a combination of the sub-cases we study. Their combination requires the individual understanding of each phenomenon and the synthesis. e.g. induced convection.
Individual project on a topic chosen by the student promotes free, creative thinking and autonomous work.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the unified presentation of Transport Phenomena. Laws of conservation. Review of vectors and tensors.

Heat transport mechanisms. Thermal conduction, Fourier
VLaw. Convection, forced convection, radiation.

Setup of equations, initial and boundary conditions and solution in one dimension. Graphical solutions in 2d with known boundary conditions. Macroscopic balance. Simple example of time-dependent heat transport under assumptions e.g. lumped capacitance method.

Fluid statics. Viscosity. Momentum transfer. Flow lines. Macroscopic balance. Mechanical energy 
V Bernoulli equation. Reynolds Transport Theorem. Dimensional analysis. Microscopic momentum balance for laminar isothermal flow. Simple solutions in Cartesian and non-Cartesian coordinate systems.
Mass transfer. Diffusion. Molecular description. Macroscopic balance. Microscopic balance of mass flow in laminar flow.
teaching_methods: Use of open-source software with example data
Online mathematical tools for solving/plotting solutions
Use of e-class for distribution of lecture notes, videos, links, questionnaires, suggested and solved exercises

assessment_methods.method: Three midterms (one at the end of each conceptual unit: heat, momentum, mass transfer)

assessment_rules: Summative assessment includes three midterms (one at the end of each conceptual unit) and a final written exam. An optional project is also offered. The detailed assessment is provided on the first day of the course and referenced in the e-class.
